result.summary: This keyboard is mostly made of ABS plastic keycaps, an aluminum case, and mechanical switches.

parts.name: Keycaps
parts.process_detail: Molten ABS is injected into molds to form keycaps with legends added via doubleshot or printing.
parts.fun_fact: Doubleshot keycaps use two colors of plastic molded together so legends never wear off.

parts.name: Mechanical switch
parts.process_detail: Housing, stem, and spring are molded and stamped separately then assembled with metal contacts.
parts.fun_fact: Cherry MX switches are rated for 50 million keystrokes, about 17 years of typical use.

parts.name: Top case
parts.process_detail: Aluminum block is CNC milled to create the frame with mounting holes and anodized.
parts.fun_fact: CNC milled aluminum cases can take over an hour to machine from a solid block.

parts.name: PCB
parts.process_detail: Copper traces are etched onto fiberglass board then components are soldered by machine.
parts.fun_fact: Keyboard PCBs use diodes at each switch to prevent ghosting when multiple keys are pressed.

parts.name: Stabilizer bar
parts.process_detail: Steel wire is drawn to precise diameter then bent to shape for stabilizing long keys.
parts.fun_fact: Stabilizers prevent long keys like the spacebar from wobbling by balancing both ends equally.

parts.name: Spacebar keycap
parts.process_detail: PBT is injection molded into long keycap shape with reinforcement ribs underneath for strength.
parts.fun_fact: PBT plastic resists shine from finger oils better than ABS and has a textured feel.

parts.name: Rotary encoder knob
parts.process_detail: Aluminum is turned on a lathe then knurled for grip and anodized for finish.
parts.fun_fact: Rotary encoders can detect infinite rotation unlike potentiometers which have physical stops.

parts.name: Bottom case
parts.process_detail: Milled from aluminum block to match top case with screw holes and rubber feet recesses.
parts.fun_fact: Aluminum cases act as heat sinks and add weight for stability during aggressive typing.

parts.name: USB controller chip
parts.process_detail: Microcontroller chip is surface mounted to PCB and handles key scanning and USB communication.
parts.fun_fact: Most mechanical keyboards use ATmega32U4 chips running QMK firmware for full programmability.

journey.title: Material sourcing
journey.detail: Aluminum ingots, plastic pellets, copper sheets, and silicon wafers are procured from suppliers.

journey.title: Component manufacturing
journey.detail: Cases are CNC milled, keycaps injection molded, switches assembled, and PCBs fabricated separately.

journey.title: PCB population
journey.detail: Switches are soldered to PCB along with controller chip and other electronic components.

journey.title: Final assembly
journey.detail: PCB with switches is mounted in case, stabilizers installed, and keycaps pressed onto switches.

journey.title: Quality control
journey.detail: Each key is tested for proper actuation and USB connectivity is verified.

journey.title: Packaging and delivery
journey.detail: Keyboard is boxed with accessories and shipped to retailers or directly to customers.
